root_cause.text: The Xilinx XDMA driver initialized `regmap_config.max_register` to the register region size (`XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN`) instead of the last valid register offset, so regmap debugfs could generate reads past the MMIO-mapped range and fault on an invalid address.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `max_register` from `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN` to `XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET` defined as `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN - 4`, and the CVE/commit message states that the wrong value “is assigned the size of the register memory region instead of the offset of the last register,” causing a segmentation fault when reading `/sys/kernel/debug/regmap/xdma.1.auto/registers`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a maximum register offset constant to constrain register accesses within the exposed register space.
intent_record.what: A new macro definition, `XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET`, was added and set to `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN - 4` immediately after the existing `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN` definition.
intent_record.how: This introduces an explicit upper bound for register offsets, limiting the maximum valid register access to the last 32-bit aligned word within the exposed register space and preventing accesses beyond the mapped range.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the regmap maximum register bound to use the correct XDMA register offset limit.
intent_record.what: In the xdma_regmap_config structure, the .max_register field was changed from XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN to XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET.
intent_record.how: This alters the highest register offset accepted by the regmap configuration, so register accesses are now bounded by XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET instead of the full register space length constant. At runtime, this can prevent regmap from treating addresses beyond the intended maximum register offset as valid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the regmap configuration: `static const struct regmap_config xdma_regmap_config = { ... .reg_stride = 4, .max_register = XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN, };`. This sets `max_register` to the register region size rather than the last valid register offset, matching the root cause. There is no compensating fix in this snippet (e.g. no `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN - 4` or equivalent bound adjustment), so regmap debugfs could still attempt reads past the mapped MMIO range.
